notes: Per-operation cost = warm seconds / rows; each width is measured at two row counts. Conversions cross the Python boundary once per value (marshalling included); the arithmetic rows are one native batch call per measurement (operands prebuilt in the 'build' phase, results freed natively).

Backends: cpu (native C), cpu-i64 / cpu-i128 (checked fixed width: refuse on overflow), cpu-wide192 (exact 192-bit accumulation), cpu-bigint (arbitrary precision), cpu-gfp4+crt (four 62-bit residues and Chinese remaindering), cuda (an actual device, --device only), and the baselines python (Python int / Fraction), numpy-int64 (wraps silently), numpy-float64 (rounds).
Python's float(Fraction) and NumPy's division round to nearest: they are timing baselines, not enclosures; the native enclosures are tight and certified.
